description: Stage 2: make the build machine trustworthy. Root cause of the failed first CI run (run 35422661722, no jobs started): .github/workflows/build.yml uses the runner context inside the job-level env block, where GitHub only allows the github, needs, strategy, matrix, vars, secrets and inputs contexts, so GitHub rejected the whole workflow. Story 1 gives ci_verify.sh a build-status mode so Ralph can see CI failures. Story 2 fixes the workflow and iterates against real CI until the build is green. Each CI check can take up to 25 minutes. Later stages are specified only after a Ralph report.

userStories.title: ci_verify.sh --build-status: pass only if the CI build for the current commit succeeded, and show why not
userStories.description: Add a --build-status mode to .ralph/ci_verify.sh. The existing test-filter mode stays unchanged. Exit 0 only if the workflow run for the current HEAD concluded success. A failing unit-test step that is marked continue-on-error must not count as a build failure.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: ci_verify.sh --build-status finds the workflow run for the current HEAD (pushing and waiting exactly like the existing mode when there is none) and exits 0 if and only if that run's conclusion is success

AC2: on any other outcome it exits 1 and prints the run URL, the conclusion, every job with its conclusion, the name of each failed step, and the last 80 lines of the failed job's log (fetched with GITHUB_TOKEN)
AC3: if the run has zero jobs it says explicitly that GitHub started no jobs, which means the workflow file itself was rejected, and prints the run URL where GitHub shows the reason
AC4: --dry-run works together with --build-status and makes no network call
AC5: existing test-filter behavior is unchanged, bash -n passes, and no token value appears anywhere in the script
userStories.notes: AC1: --build-status reuses the existing mode's run lookup/push/wait (unchanged code path) and exits 0 iff CONCL == success; any other completed conclusion goes to the reporter. AC2: reporter prints run URL + 'NOT success: conclusion=<c>', then every job with its conclusion, then for each non-success/non-neutral/non-skipped job the failing/cancelled step names and the last 80 lines of that job's log via GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs (GITHUB_TOKEN only, never a file; temp dir mktemp + EXIT trap). AC3: JOB_COUNT==0 prints 'GitHub started NO jobs ... workflow file itself was rejected' + run URL before exiting 1. AC4: --build-status --dry-run does zero network (verified tokenless exit 0). AC5: filter mode untouched (re-verified pass/fail/no-match verdicts end-to-end against a fake curl harness); bash -n clean; no token-prefix literal in the 4 scanned tooling files. FIXED pre-existing latent bug in pick_run_id: `python3 - <<'PY'` heredoc consumed the pipeline stdin so json.load(sys.stdin) read the python source, meaning the run lookup could never work for real (would have blocked CI-GREEN-BUILD) — the piped JSON now travels via RUN_JSON_PAYLOAD env var. Verified against a fake curl: success run exit 0; failure run exit 1 with URL/jobs/failed-step/log-tail; zero-jobs exit 1 with rejection message.

userStories.title: The debug APK builds green on GitHub Actions
userStories.description: Get the debug APK build green on GitHub Actions. Known cause of the first failure: in .github/workflows/build.yml the job-level env block uses runner.temp, and the runner context is not allowed there. Move ANDROID_HOME and ANDROID_SDK_ROOT into a step (write them to GITHUB_ENV, using runner.temp inside the step where it is allowed) or use a fixed path. After that, iterate against real CI: results come back through ci_verify.sh --build-status. Fix what it reports, one root cause at a time.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: the workflow no longer references the runner or env context in any job-level env value
AC2: ci_verify.sh --build-status exits 0 for the HEAD commit, meaning the Build debug APK step and the artifact upload steps succeeded on GitHub
AC3: the unit test step stays continue-on-error, and the baseline counts (tests, failures, errors, skipped) from the job summary are copied into this story's notes
AC4: every failure found along the way is recorded in the notes as one line each (cause and fix), so the same kind of failure is quick to recognize next time

AC5: no Kotlin source is edited to make CI pass; if the only way forward needs a source or dependency decision, stop and write it under a clear heading in progress.txt instead of stubbing or disabling modules
AC6: change at most one root cause per commit so CI feedback stays attributable
